relevance_note: Case report of a GFAP mutation carrier: 'Analysis of the GFAPgene revealed a heterozygous missense mutation, c.827G>T, p.R276L'.
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON from values I chose. One first-hand patient (the case report, label 'patient'). Five previously published people from the Discussion were kept because each has an individual-level fact beyond diagnosis: ref [11] patient (variant c.827G>T, p.R276L), patient 1 of ref [21] (parkinsonism), ref [22] patient (symmetrical striatal lesions), ref [30] patient (asymptomatic carrier over age 60), ref [32] patient (valproate-induced parkinsonism). Left out: the E223Q person of ref [38] (variant now classified as a polymorphism, dismissed by the authors; not given an Alexander disease diagnosis here); features cited only to a reference without saying it is one person ('diffuse bradykinesia [22]', 'rigidity of the arms [29]', 'spotty lesions [19]', 'bilateral lesions in the lateral putamen [30]'), which were not attached to anyone. Table 1 holds only group counts of the literature cases and gives no rows. No variant row for ref [30] patient: the sentence says 'carrier' but does not name the gene or variant. Main patient: age at onset left 'not reported' because the authors attribute the first changes after the head trauma at 46 (character change, dementia) to the contusion and never state an age at onset of Alexander disease; feature onsets are recorded per feature. Contradictions/inconsistencies: the Case Presentation says 'heterogeneous missense mutation' while the Abstract and Discussion say 'heterozygous'; zygosity taken from the latter. The text says 'slight cerebral atrophy' while the Figure 1 legend says 'moderate cortical atrophy with ventricular enlargement'; both recorded as separate features. 'Cerebellar ataxia was ambiguous' so no ataxia row and the ataxia checklist item is 'not reported'; gaze-evoked nystagmus is recorded under eye movement abnormality only. Laboratory tests 'unremarkable' were recorded as one excluded feature worded as the paper names the tests (D-27), excluding nothing more specific. 'Contrast enhancement on MRI' left 'not reported': the only statement is that the globus pallidus signal change had no contrast enhancement (narrower than the checklist item), recorded as its own excluded feature. Cerebral white matter abnormality marked observed from the deep white matter lacunae, although leukoencephalopathy was explicitly not seen. Parkinsonism in the main patient is only hedged ('presumably caused a rigid-bradykinesia type parkinsonism') and was not recorded. No stacked cells in this paper.
